the current findings attest to significant challenges experienced by the college students who experienced the changes in their learning conditions due to the COVID 19 outbreak.

this study provides evidence that the adaptability of students to the sudden transition to synchronous online teaching during the COVID 10 pandemic is associated with positive reactions to online learning and that personality traits play a significant role in the process

this paper provides evidence that students who were more adaptable to the pandemic were more likely to have a positive attitude and learning experience in the online environment, and that this relationship was mediated by their personality and sense of belonging and matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the COVID 19 crisis has brought to the forefront the importance of adaptability in the face of uncertainty and rapid change, and the importance of the social environment for the well being of students
we have shown that adaptability to a sudden change in the learning environment is a key factor in how well students adjust to a transition to online learning.
we found that the personality trait of adaptability is related to positive learning experiences in online education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adaptability is a key factor in how students respond to the changes and challenges brought about by the pandemic.

adaptability is a crucial factor in how students react to the changes in their learning conditions due to the pandemic, which is consistent with previous work on how students cope with the changes in their lives during the pandemic (Kaplowitz & Ehrmann, 2020)

the transition to online learning due to COVID 19 was challenging for many college students, and those who were more adaptable to the pandemic had better reactions to online learning, and in turn, more positive learning experiences.
